title: Aave Approves Deprecation of 50 Assets and Exit From Six Chains
dek: Aave governance approved deprecation of 50 low-adoption asset reserves and full withdrawal from six blockchain deployments (Sonic, Scroll, zkSync, Metis, Soneium, Aptos), affecting $98.1 million in supplied assets, per The Defiant. The consolidation reflects the protocol's focus shift toward high-value markets and risk reduction as operational complexity threatens profitability.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: Aave is retiring 50 assets and exiting six chains that generate under $5,000 per quarter in protocol revenue each, with affected positions representing less than 1% of the protocol's $14.3 billion total deposits.
bottom_line: Watch for the formal onchain vote timeline and gauge governance approval momentum; the proposal still requires a binding vote before implementation. The story's validity depends on how quickly suppliers exit the retiring chains and whether the deprecation mechanism forces orderly liquidations or meets resistance. If adoption on V4 accelerates while deprecated assets drain, the consolidation thesis holds; if V4 growth stalls, it signals user adoption may be more fragmented than the protocol expects.
body: Aave governance approved deprecation of 50 low-adoption asset reserves and full withdrawal from six blockchain deployments, according to The Defiant. The affected chains are Sonic, Scroll, zkSync, Metis, Soneium, and Aptos. The consolidation impacts $98.1 million in supplied assets and $15.6 million in outstanding debt, less than 1 percent of Aave's $14.3 billion total deposits across all deployments.

The deprecation targets 50 individual asset reserves plus 21 matured Pendle principal tokens held across eleven deployments, accounting for $85.3 million in supply. Six whole-market shutdowns cover 25 reserves with $12.8 million in supplied assets. Each of the six retiring chains generates under $5,000 per quarter in protocol revenue, below the cost of maintaining oracles, monitoring, and operational support, per The Defiant's reporting.

The adoption collapse on these chains has been steep: Sonic deposits fell 74 percent over six months to $7.6 million; Scroll deposits dropped 86 percent to $2.2 million; zkSync fell 88 percent to $844,000; and Soneium declined 95 percent to $173,000, according to the protocol's data.

The deprecation mechanism works by freezing each reserve, dropping supply and borrow caps to 1, and raising reserve factors to 99 percent on the six retiring deployments alongside a 5 percent base borrow rate. This approach discourages new borrowing and incentivizes suppliers to withdraw and borrowers to repay without abruptly shutting markets, per The Defiant. The proposal is an Aave Request for Final Comment (ARFC) preceding a binding onchain vote.

Aave is also offboarding reserves flagged for Chainlink price feed risk, including LUSD, FRAX, and RPL on Ethereum. The protocol adopted a new Risk Framework setting usage thresholds each listed asset must justify against its fixed operational load. Founder Stani Kulechov stated the move should not be interpreted as a vote against any L1 or L2, but rather designed to reduce Aave's operational, technical, and economic risk surface, per The Defiant.

The biggest individual positions in scope are two Bitcoin liquid-staking wrappers on Ethereum, FBTC and eBTC, which hold a combined $16.3 million after supplied balances collapsed from roughly $72 million six months prior. Bridged tokens including USDC.e and USDbC are removed where native versions exist. MaticX is wound down because issuer Stader is sunsetting the token.
Meanwhile, Aave V4 deposits nearly doubled over the past month, with caps raised for the eleventh time, according to The Defiant. AAVE token traded at $98.61, up 0.5 percent in the past 24 hours.
